S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) is characterized by developmentally inappropriate levels of motor activity, restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty inhibiting actions, with relatively fewer prominent inattentive symptoms. Adults may present with chronic inner restlessness, difficulty staying seated, excessive talking, and interrupting others, often leading to occupational, relational, or legal problems. Symptoms typically begin in childhood, but in some individuals they become clinically significant or are first recognized later in life when environmental demands change or compensatory strategies fail. It is distinguished from mood, anxiety, and personality disorders by its early onset, pervasive pattern across settings, and specific profile of hyperactive-impulsive behaviors rather than episodic or situational agitation.

patient.stressor: Over the past year, Nilda shifted from mostly solo surveillance work to a contract with a large law firm that requires her to spend long hours in conference rooms reviewing files and sitting through structured case conferences. For the first time in her career, she has to remain in one place for extended periods, follow rigid meeting agendas, and sit quietly while senior partners talk through strategy, which clashes with the more mobile, self‑paced style she has always relied on. Over the last eight months, her difficulty tolerating these new demands has started to interfere with her reputation for calm professionalism, drawing comments from colleagues about her restlessness and making her worry that she will lose this lucrative contract. After an uncomfortable incident where a partner pulled her aside to ask if she was "bored or anxious" during a key meeting, she became concerned enough about how out of control her behavior felt compared to her disciplined self‑image that she agreed, at the urging of a younger mentee who has ADHD, to seek a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: “In these long client and attorney meetings, I just can’t stay in my seat—I keep having to get up and move around even when I know it looks unprofessional.”

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: In those long conference room sessions, I’m constantly bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, or twisting in my chair without even realizing it until I see the paralegal next to me inch her notebook away from my jittering.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: During these strategy meetings, I keep inventing reasons to stand up—refilling my water, checking something on the printer, pretending I need a file from my bag—because staying planted in that chair for more than twenty minutes makes me feel like I’m crawling out of my skin, even though I know it looks bad.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even at home, if I try to wind down with a movie or read a novel, I end up talking over it, commenting on every little thing, or pacing around the living room because just sitting there quietly feels almost impossible.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My family teases me that I never just ‘sit and be’—I’m always pacing, sorting something, checking my email, or planning the next thing, and if I do sit down for a bit I pop right back up like there’s a motor in me.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: In meetings and even casual conversations, I catch myself barreling on with every detail of a stakeout or theory about a case long after people’s eyes glaze over, and I have to consciously force myself to shut up.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I have this bad habit in the firm’s case conferences of jumping in while the partners are still talking, finishing their sentences, or blurting out my ideas before they’re done, and only afterward do I realize I basically steamrolled the room.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_12_years: Ever since elementary school I was the kid who couldn’t stay in my seat, constantly getting notes sent home because I’d be up wandering the classroom or blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over these past several months, my restlessness and interrupting in the firm’s long meetings have led to partners pulling me aside about my ‘unprofessional’ behavior, and I’m genuinely worried it’s putting this major contract—and my reputation as steady and composed—at risk.
add_requirements.duration: These problems have really come to a head over the last eight months or so, ever since I started this contract that requires those long, sit-still conference room sessions.
